Definition: Does the government maintain a digital business register?
Comments: Digital business registry services exist: the Fichier National RCCM provides online search/consultation of official company documents; additional online services exist for RCCM acts and beneficial ownership register (RBE).
revision_notes: Verified all three original sources. The RBE (beneficial ownership) source (servicepublic.gov.bf) returned an HTTP 403 error and could not be directly fetched, but its existence is corroborated by other government references. The FN RCCM platform (fichiernationalrccm.bf) was officially launched online on 28 December 2023 as a nationwide register, holding over 232,000 files at launch and currently listing 80,604 registered businesses, confirming nationwide search/consultation coverage. However, the transactional e-actes-rccm.gov.bf service, used to request and issue RCCM certificates and extracts online, explicitly states it currently covers only businesses registered at the Tribunal de Commerce de Ouagadougou, meaning full transactional e-services are not yet nationwide. This supports 'Partially deployed' rather than 'Fully deployed nationwide'. Score confirmed at 4.
revised_comments: Burkina Faso operates a national digital business register, the Fichier National du Registre de Commerce et du Crédit Mobilier (FN RCCM), launched online on 28 December 2023 and accessible at fichiernationalrccm.bf, providing free public search and consultation of over 80,000 registered businesses nationwide. A companion online service, e-actes-rccm.gov.bf, allows requests for RCCM extracts and certificates, though this transactional service currently covers only businesses registered with the Tribunal de Commerce de Ouagadougou. A dedicated online beneficial ownership register (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) is also referenced on the government e-services portal. The register is therefore digitally accessible nationwide for search purposes, but full transactional e-service delivery remains partial.

Definition: Is the register integrated with the government's national data exchange system?
Comments: Interoperability is described between civil registration and health facilities (births registered from maternity wards into central system; interoperability activities referenced by partners), but not confirmed as nationwide full DPI integration.
revision_notes: Both original sources verified. The iCivil source describes an operational, not merely planned, data linkage: midwives register births directly from maternity wards into the central civil registration system in real time, using smartphones and unique 'bubble code' identifiers, having moved beyond pilot stage in Ouagadougou with plans to expand nationwide. The AMADE (2024-ongoing) source confirms a current project to 'test and document the implementation of an automated birth registration system through digitisation and interoperability with health services' in additional municipalities, indicating the integration is an active, expanding pilot rather than a merely planned initiative. No evidence was found of the civil register being connected to a broader, cross-agency national government data exchange platform (e.g. an X-Road/GovStack-type system); the demonstrated integration is specifically with health facilities. Score revised upward from 'Planned' (2) to 'Under development' (3) to reflect the operational pilot, but not to 'Partially integrated' given the narrow, health-sector-only and still-expanding scope.
revised_comments: Burkina Faso's civil registration system includes an operational digital interoperability mechanism (iCivil) linking maternity wards to the central civil registration database, enabling real-time birth registration by midwives using smartphones and unique identifiers. Originally piloted in ten maternity wards in Ouagadougou with UNFPA support, the platform is being expanded with the stated aim of eventual nationwide coverage. A further initiative running from 2024 aims to test and document automated birth registration through digitisation and interoperability with health services in additional municipalities. This represents a targeted, health-sector data exchange mechanism under active development, rather than a fully-fledged connection to a broader national government data exchange platform.

Definition: Does the government maintain a digital electoral register?
Comments: Electoral register exists with biometric voter registration introduced in 2012; lists published and consultable (at least via CENI website/posted lists), but not clearly a full online searchable register.
revision_notes: Original sources (2012-13) described only the initial biometric enrolment exercise and were outdated. A 2020 independent international audit of the Burkina Faso biometric electoral register (conducted jointly by the OIF and African Union, published as a press communiqué) found a functioning, continuously-updated biometric database covering 6,490,926 registered voters, with enrolment completed in 329 of 351 communes (94%) and 7,694 of 9,299 villages (83%), plus active deduplication removing 1,425,725 duplicate records. This is a mature, near-nationwide biometric digital electoral register, well beyond 'Under development'. Score revised upward from 3 to 4 ('Partially deployed') on this basis, not to 5 given incomplete geographic coverage. However, in July 2025 the transitional military government dissolved the CENI, the body that had run the register since 2001, transferring electoral responsibilities to the Ministry of Territorial Administration, with elections deferred until at least 2029. This creates material uncertainty about whether the register is still being actively maintained/updated under the new arrangement, so this row is flagged for human review rather than treated as a settled current-state assessment.
revised_comments: Burkina Faso has maintained a biometric digital electoral register since 2012, updated through periodic exceptional revisions. An independent international audit conducted by the Organisation internationale de la Francophonie and the African Union in October 2020 found the register held 6,490,926 voters, with biometric enrolment completed in 94% of communes and 83% of villages nationwide, alongside substantial deduplication work to ensure the uniqueness of registered electors. Administration of the register has since been affected by institutional change: in July 2025 the transitional government dissolved the Independent National Electoral Commission (CENI), which had managed the register, transferring electoral responsibilities to the Ministry of Territorial Administration, with no elections scheduled before 2029.

Definition: Does the government maintain one or more social protection registers?
Comments: A national digital social registry exists: Registre Social Unique (RSU), adopted by decree in 2021 and operational with household/individual records for targeting social programs.
revision_notes: Original World Bank source confirmed and read; rsu.gov.bf returned an HTTP 403 error and could not be directly fetched, but its existence and role are corroborated by extensive government and press reporting. Additional reporting confirms the Registre Social Unique (RSU) completed a pilot phase in the Centre-Est and Centre-Ouest regions (finalised 2024, registering over 215,000 poor/vulnerable households) and has since expanded to further areas, including a 2025 targeting and enumeration exercise in Ouahigouya (Nord region) registering over 16,000 households. This confirms the register is digitally operational and actively expanding region by region but has not yet achieved full national coverage, consistent with 'Partially deployed'. Score confirmed at 4.
revised_comments: Burkina Faso maintains a digital social protection registry, the Registre Social Unique (RSU), which collects and centralises socioeconomic data on poor and vulnerable households and individuals to target social protection programmes, assigning each registered person a unique identification code. Following a pilot phase in the Centre-Est and Centre-Ouest regions completed in 2024 (registering over 215,000 households), the RSU has continued to expand to additional areas, including a 2025 targeting and enumeration exercise in Ouahigouya in the Nord region that registered over 16,000 households. The register is supported by the World Bank-financed Sahel Adaptive Social Protection Program and forms a core instrument of the National Social Protection Strategy 2024-2028, though national coverage remains partial as the rollout continues region by region.
